While classic paella is made with white rice, I’ve chosen Spanish-grown pearl barley for its unique blend of nutrition and sustainability. Compared to brown rice, barley offers more fiber (about 6g per cooked cup vs. 3.5g in brown rice) and a lower glycemic index, meaning it digests more slowly and helps keep you full longer. Farro, another Mediterranean favorite, is also rich in fiber and protein, but is often imported and can require more water to cultivate, depending on the variety and origin.

From an environmental perspective, barley is well-suited to Spain’s increasingly dry climate, requiring less irrigation than rice and often grown in rotation with other crops to support soil health. Brown rice, while more nutritious than white rice, still tends to have a higher water footprint and is less commonly grown locally. Farro’s environmental impact varies, but it’s less widely available from Spanish producers.
